question: Explain the doctrine of indoor management and the exceptions to it.

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Outsiders dealing with a company in good faith may assume that its internal procedures have been complied with; they need not inquire into internal regularity.

points.label: Origin and purpose
points.description: Laid down in Royal British Bank v. Turquand; it protects outsiders and limits the doctrine of constructive notice.

points.label: Exception: knowledge of irregularity
points.description: It does not protect an outsider who actually knew of the irregularity.

points.label: Exception: negligence or suspicion
points.description: It does not apply where the outsider ignored suspicious circumstances that called for inquiry, or where the document relied on is forged.

points.label: Exception: acts beyond authority
points.description: It does not cover acts outside the company's powers or the apparent authority of the officer, or cases where the outsider had not relied on the articles.
